tool_usage.tool_name: Qualcomm in-house on-device AI code-generation assistant (LLaMA 3 8B on Snapdragon NPU, integrated with Visual Studio)
what_for: On-device code generation in the IDE (Visual Studio) for Qualcomm's own software engineers
Generating/assisting with code while keeping proprietary source off cloud/hyperscaler models (IP protection)
Doubling as a reference/demo of Snapdragon X NPU on-device coding capability for enterprise customers
tool_usage.teams: unknown (described broadly as Qualcomm engineers; demoed by Jeff Monday, VP Global Enterprise & Channel Sales)
tool_usage.scale: Reported 1,500+ Qualcomm engineers and 'millions of lines of code' (per a Qualcomm-VP CIO.com demo video, ~June 2025). CAVEAT: figure comes from a single demo/promotional source surfaced via search summaries; exact wording not directly verifiable (primary pages returned HTTP 403).
tool_usage.confidence_note: Medium. Multiple consistent search-result returns attribute the in-house tool + 1,500-engineer figure to the same CIO demo/Qualcomm VP, which is a credible primary-ish source (a Qualcomm executive). However it is a promotional product-demo context and the exact number could not be confirmed verbatim due to 403 fetch blocks. Confident that Qualcomm uses an in-house on-device AI coding assistant internally; less certain on precise scale.

tool_usage.tool_name: Qualcomm Verilog/HDL code-generation LLMs (fine-tuned LLaMA 3.1 8B on in-house IP)
what_for: Generating Verilog/HDL for chip design using models fine-tuned on Qualcomm in-house IP validated through tape-outs
Evaluating external specialized Verilog models (e.g., NYU Tandon CL Verilog) for potential internal/commercial use
tool_usage.confidence_note: Low-medium. Evidence is from academic papers / research news indicating Qualcomm engineers fine-tune LLMs on in-house Verilog IP and receive specialized models for evaluation. Shows applied interest in LLM code generation for HDL, but no quantified internal deployment or production-workflow detail.

tool_usage.tool_name: CodeMate (third-party agentic coding agent on Snapdragon X)
what_for: CodeMate's end-to-end AI coding agent (write/secure/quality-gate code in IDE; automate code review and security analysis across GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps) running ON-DEVICE on Snapdragon X-Series
Showcasing on-device AI coding for developers, students, institutions (India Mobile Congress 2025)
tool_usage.teams: n/a — Qualcomm is the silicon/platform partner; CodeMate AI is the vendor
tool_usage.confidence_note: High that this is a product/ISV integration (CodeMate runs on Snapdragon hardware), NOT evidence that Qualcomm engineers use CodeMate internally. Included to flag product_integration noise vs internal dogfooding.

tool_usage.tool_name: Contextual AI RAG engineering assistant (NOT a coding tool)
what_for: Querying and synthesizing dense internal + external technical documentation to speed up resolving customer engineering issues
tool_usage.teams: Customer Engineering / broader engineering org (VP of Engineering Yogi Chiniga)
tool_usage.scale: 'thousands of engineers' in daily workflows as of Nov 2024 (vendor case study)
tool_usage.confidence_note: Medium for the documentation-assistant claim (vendor case study, not directly fetchable / 403). Explicitly NOT an agentic coding/developer tool — included for completeness and to avoid miscounting it as a coding assistant.

notes: Primary takeaway: Qualcomm's clearest internal use of an AI coding tool is its OWN in-house on-device code-generation assistant (LLaMA 3 8B on Snapdragon NPU, in Visual Studio), used by a reported 1,500+ engineers for millions of lines of code, deliberately on-device to protect proprietary IP from cloud/hyperscaler models. There is also applied use of fine-tuned LLMs for Verilog/HDL chip-design code. NO evidence was found of Qualcomm internally adopting named third-party agentic coding agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot agent mode/Workspace, OpenAI Codex/Operator, Amazon Q Developer, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor, Devin, Windsurf, Cowork). CodeMate is a Snapdragon product/ISV integration, not internal use; Contextual AI is an internal documentation RAG assistant, not a coding tool. Several key source pages (cio.com, contextual.ai, LinkedIn, starthub) returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch, so figures rely on consistent search-result summaries — treat exact numbers with mild caution.
